entries.appliesTo: health insurers, HMOs, and dental preferred provider plan insurers (including their third party contractors) that downcode health benefits claims; providers submitting claims

dutySources.disclosure-ui: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 9(c) — 'An insurer must disclose in an easily accessible and readable manner when artificial intelligence is used to: (1) make an adverse determination on a prior authorization request; or (2) downcode a claim.'
dutySources.human-review: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 9(a) — 'An insurer may not use an automated: (1) process; (2) system; or (3) tool, including artificial intelligence; as the sole basis to downcode a claim based on medical necessity without the review of the covered individual's medical record by an employee or contractor of the insurer.'
dutySources.takedown-process: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 12(a) — 'An insurer shall provide providers with a clear and accessible process for appealing downcoded claims'

sources.humanReview: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 9(a) — 'without the review of the covered individual's medical record by an employee or contractor of the insurer'
sources.disclosure: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 9(c) — 'An insurer must disclose in an easily accessible and readable manner when artificial intelligence is used'
sources.aiSoleBasis: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 9(a) — 'may not use an automated: (1) process; (2) system; or (3) tool, including artificial intelligence; as the sole basis to downcode a claim based on medical necessity'
sources.appealDays: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 12(a)(3) — 'a timeline for submission of an appeal that is not less than one hundred eighty (180) days'

flags: No penalty or enforcement provision in the downcoding chapter; Sec. 14 grants rulemaking only: 'The department shall adopt rules under IC 4-22-2 to carry out this chapter.' Contrast the hospital chapter, where IC 16-21-9.5 Sec. 8 says 'administer and enforce this chapter' and Sec. 9 sets a civil penalty — the AI chapter deliberately omits both. Exposure omitted (silence is silence); rulemaking is not enforcement.

Omnibus insurance/hospital bill: only IC 27-1-52 (SECTION 6, downcoding) contains AI provisions. Non-AI provisions coded nowhere: IC 16-21-9.5 hospital payment-assistance-program notices (with state department civil penalty 'of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000) per violation' deposited to the state general fund), downcoding notice via CARC/RARC codes (Sec. 11), no downcoding based solely on diagnosis code (Sec. 10), no targeted/discriminatory downcoding (Sec. 13), 60-day notice before CPT rate reductions (IC 27-8-5.7-6.7, IC 27-13-36.2-4.7), 180-day recoupment and 3-year audit limits (IC 27-8-5.7-10, IC 27-13-36.2-8), and coordination-of-benefits resubmission rights (IC 27-8-5.7-11.5, IC 27-13-36.2-9.5).

decisionsCovered fits no enum: the AI provisions cover claim downcoding and adverse prior authorization determinations ('make an adverse determination on a prior authorization request; or (2) downcode a claim'), not denials generally; param omitted rather than coded lossy.

Sec. 9(b) also binds providers: 'A provider may not use an automated: (1) process; (2) system; or (3) tool, including artificial intelligence; to submit a health benefits claim without the review of a provider or other person involved in the development of the claim for submission.'
Chapter scope exclusion, Sec. 0.3: 'This chapter does not apply to the Medicaid program or a managed care organization (as defined in IC 12-7-2-126.9) that provides services to a Medicaid recipient.'
appealDays (180) applies to appeals of all downcoded claims, not only AI-driven downcoding; batch appeals of similar claims must be allowed (Sec. 12(b)).
